ap_macroeconomics-f01.title: Interest rates, the exchange rate, and net exports

stimulus.description: Data for Brevonia, a country with a floating exchange rate and a banking system with ample reserves (billions of dollars).

notes: Between Year 1 and Year 2 the central bank of Brevonia raised its administered interest rates to reduce inflationary pressure. Its currency is the ora.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the foreign exchange market for the ora (the currency of Brevonia), showing the equilibrium exchange rate labeled ER1 and the equilibrium quantity of ora labeled Q1.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Downward-sloping demand for ora and upward-sloping supply of ora, with the exchange rate on the vertical axis and the quantity of ora on the horizontal axis, intersecting at ER1 and Q1.

required_elements: Draws a downward-sloping demand curve and an upward-sloping supply curve for the ora, labels the vertical axis as the exchange rate (units of foreign currency per ora) and the horizontal axis as the quantity of ora
alt_solutions: curves may be labeled D and S
axis may say exchange rate or price of the currency
common_errors: labels the vertical axis as the price level
draws two curves with the same slope sign
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Labels the intersection of the two curves with the equilibrium exchange rate ER1 on the vertical axis and Q1 on the horizontal axis
alt_solutions: dashed lines from the intersection to both axes
labels the point E1 with ER1 and Q1
common_errors: labels a point that is not the intersection
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify the effect of the central bank's higher administered interest rates on net financial capital inflows to Brevonia.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Net financial capital inflows increase (foreign investors want more of the country's higher-yielding assets).

required_elements: States that net financial capital inflows to the country increase
alt_solutions: more foreign investment in the country's financial assets
capital flows into the country rise
common_errors: says net financial capital inflows decrease
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: On your graph from part (A), show the effect of the change in net financial capital flows on the market for the ora: label the new exchange rate ER2.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. The demand for the ora shifts to the right (or, equivalently, the supply of the ora shifts to the left because domestic investors buy fewer foreign assets), and the new equilibrium exchange rate ER2 is higher than ER1.

required_elements: Shifts the demand curve for the ora to the right or the supply curve of the ora to the left, and labels the new curve
alt_solutions: arrow showing the rightward shift of demand
a leftward shift of supply because domestic investors buy fewer foreign assets
common_errors: shifts the supply curve to the right
shifts the demand curve to the left
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Labels the new equilibrium exchange rate ER2 above ER1 at the intersection of the new demand curve and the supply curve
alt_solutions: dashed line to the vertical axis at ER2
the ora appreciates on the graph
common_errors: labels ER2 at the old intersection
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Based on the change in the value of the ora, will exports from Brevonia increase, decrease, or stay the same? Explain.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Exports decrease, because the appreciation of the ora makes the country's goods more expensive for foreign buyers.

required_elements: States that exports decrease because the stronger currency makes the country's goods more expensive to foreign buyers
alt_solutions: appreciation raises the foreign price of exports
foreigners buy fewer of the country's goods
common_errors: says exports are unaffected by the exchange rate
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, calculate net exports in Year 1 and in Year 2, and show your work.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Net exports in Year 1 = 700 - 640 = 60 billion; net exports in Year 2 = 620 - 680 = -60 billion.

required_elements: Subtracts imports from exports in Year 1 to get net exports (the Year 1 answer is correct)
alt_solutions: exports minus imports for Year 1
the same numerical answer in an equivalent form (fraction, decimal, or with units)
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Subtracts imports from exports in Year 2 to get net exports (the Year 2 answer is correct)
alt_solutions: exports minus imports for Year 2
the same numerical answer in an equivalent form (fraction, decimal, or with units)
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: F
parts.prompt: Explain how the central bank's action will affect real GDP in the short run, considering both the effect of higher interest rates on spending and the effect of the change in net exports.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Higher interest rates reduce interest-sensitive consumption and investment, and the lower net exports reduce aggregate demand further, so aggregate demand shifts to the left and real GDP falls.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the reason: interest-rate effect on spending
required_elements: Explains that higher interest rates reduce interest-sensitive consumption and investment spending, which decreases aggregate demand
alt_solutions: borrowing is more expensive so spending falls
aggregate demand shifts left
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the reason: net exports reinforce the fall
required_elements: Explains that the lower net exports from the stronger currency also decrease aggregate demand, so real GDP falls
alt_solutions: net exports are a component of aggregate demand
the appreciation reinforces the contraction
common_errors: says lower net exports raise aggregate demand
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.
